SystemSketch · implementation report · 1 September 2026 · follows the state-recorder design review

The flight recorder, built

Steps 1 to 6 of the design review are in the tree and proved in a real browser: an always-armed ring buffer in the page, a Recording section in the Dev menu with Save the last 30 s, Record next ≤ 30 s and Copy last recording, a red bar during a take, a Python route that writes one folder per recording with the packet first, a Node sidecar that keeps Chrome's screencast in a ring behind one launcher flag, and a playback.html in every folder. Recording is on by default in Preview and the isolated presets, off by default in Stable, with a persisted toggle either way. Your question about the cost of the screenshots is answered with a measurement in §1.

journey 30 / 30 checks · real Chrome, real folder, real clipboard 8 buffer unit tests · 9 host unit tests · tsc clean screencast: ~16–17 ms CPU per frame, frame timing unchanged desktop windows need one relaunch to get the debugging port

1 · Your two questions

What do the screenshots cost?

Measured, not estimated: docs/recorder_screencast_cost.mjs ran the spike's 8.4 s Block gesture eight times in fresh headless instances (A B C D A B C D) and read every Chrome process's CPU time from /proc, plus frame timing from inside the page.

The screencast costs CPU, not smoothness. At the spike's setting Chrome used +18.6 percentage points of one core on top of a 24.1 % baseline while the gesture ran, and nothing when the page was idle, because Chrome only produces a frame on repaint. Frame timing inside the page did not move: rAF p50 / p95 stayed at 16.7 / 16.8 ms with and without the screencast, and the long tasks are the gesture's own. The cost is a near-constant ~16–17 ms of CPU per delivered frame whatever the size or quality, so frame count is the lever. The shipped sidecar therefore takes every second repaint at full resolution (row C is the nearest measured point: +9.7 points), which still delivers more frames than a save keeps.

Caveat: headless Chrome with the GPU disabled, so capture and JPEG encoding were all on the CPU; a GPU-backed desktop window should be cheaper in absolute terms. The relative picture — cost per frame, none at rest, no jank — is the finding. The in-page half stays at the design review's 2.1 ms per 8.4 s.

Off in Stable, on where bugs are expected — yes

Adopted exactly as you proposed. The default is decided synchronously at mount, which a retroactive recorder needs, and it is a one-liner: the app runs from the dev server in Preview and in every isolated preset, and from a built release in Stable, so import.meta.env.DEV is the channel split. A persisted toggle in the Recording section overrides it in either direction and disarms the host's screencast the moment you turn it off (proved in the journey). Stable therefore costs nothing until you opt in.

export function defaultRecorderEnabled(): boolean {
  return import.meta.env.DEV
}

export function readStoredEnabled(): boolean | null {
  try {
    const stored = window.localStorage.getItem(RECORDER_ENABLED_KEY)
    return stored === 'on' ? true : stored === 'off' ? false : null
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

The launcher opens the debugging port for both channels regardless, so opting in on Stable works without another relaunch. It is loopback-only, and Chrome refuses any browser origin on it; the sidecar connects as a plain Node client (verified against a Chrome started without any origin allow-list).

2 · What shipped, step by step

The six steps of the design review's §7, each one where the review said it would go. 2864 new lines across 10 files; the stock-boundary test still passes because nothing new sits beside the engine.

  1. The ring buffer — src/recorder/flightRecorder.tsSeven lanes on one clock (input · dom · state · menu · store · console · mark), trimmed to the window on every push. The DOM lane is the finding from the spike made real: capture-phase keydown/keyup/pointerdown on the window, with the UI element hit, so Escape into a menu is recorded even though tldraw never sees it. A retroactive save rewinds the end snapshot through the window's diffs with tldraw's own reverseRecordsDiff, so start.snapshot.json is real for both modes. Installed from onMount in the product and in the presets, never in the embedded IDE lane.
  2. Dev menu, REC bar, policy — src/recorder/RecorderControls.tsx, recorderStore.tsThe Recording section sits between Isolated presets and Version & updates, in the panel's own row grammar; window chips 5 / 15 / 30 / 60 / 120 s; a note field whose text becomes the first line of the packet; an On/Off chip. The bar is portaled onto document.body because the canvas layer sits under tldraw's top chrome. The presets get the same three verbs in a compact strip inside their identity bar.
  3. Host route and writer — scripts/server.py, scripts/recording_store.pyPOST /api/recordings writes ~/SystemSketch/recordings/<local time>-<note>/ staged then renamed, keeps the last 20, and returns the packet; GET /api/recordings/last refills the clipboard after a reload; POST /api/recordings/arm tells the host whether the page wants frames. The packet maps every state seen to the file that defines it by indexing id = '…' declarations under src/ and tldraw's tools.
  4. Frames — scripts/recorder_frames.mjs + one launcher flag--remote-debugging-port per channel (4324 Preview, 4325 Stable) on the desktop Chrome, passed to the host as --cdp-port. The host spawns the sidecar lazily when a page arms it; the sidecar attaches to every page of that Chrome, keeps a ring of screencast frames per page while armed, and on save writes the wall-time slice into the folder at one frame per 300 ms. Both files travel with a release's runtime/ and count toward the controller fingerprint.
  5. Proof — tests/recorder_smoke.mjs (npm run test:recorder)30 checks read off the disk and the DOM (§3). The harness learned to start Chrome first and hand its DevTools port to the host, the way the launcher does.
  6. playback.html per recording + state→source mapWritten into every folder by the host: frames by relative path, rows inlined, lane filters, a synthetic pointer, #t=<ms> deep links. Opens from file:// with no server.

Read these files, in this order:
1. /tmp/recorder-smoke-files-mPZqQW/SystemSketch/recordings/2026-09-01_22-26-25-cable-landed-then-the-detector-w/README.md  — this summary
2. /tmp/recorder-smoke-files-mPZqQW/SystemSketch/recordings/2026-09-01_22-26-25-cable-landed-then-the-detector-w/timeline.jsonl  — every event, one JSON object per line. `t` is ms since the start. Lanes: input (what tldraw's state chart received), dom (raw keydown/keyup/pointerdown on the window, with the UI element hit), state (state-chart path changes), menu (open menus), store (record diffs: add/update/remove with the changed keys), console (console calls and uncaught errors), mark (notes).
3. /tmp/recorder-smoke-files-mPZqQW/SystemSketch/recordings/2026-09-01_22-26-25-cable-landed-then-the-detector-w/frames/  — 12 screenshots named by ms since the start (f-001098.jpg = +1.10 s). To see what the screen showed after an event at t, open the first frame with a larger number. Chrome screencast frames: what the window actually showed, UI chrome included, no mouse pointer (the input lane has it).
4. /tmp/recorder-smoke-files-mPZqQW/SystemSketch/recordings/2026-09-01_22-26-25-cable-landed-then-the-detector-w/start.snapshot.json  — the tldraw store (document + session records) at t=0; /tmp/recorder-smoke-files-mPZqQW/SystemSketch/recordings/2026-09-01_22-26-25-cable-landed-then-the-detector-w/end.snapshot.json is the store at save time. `editor.store.loadStoreSnapshot(start)` then replaying the store lane reproduces every instant.
5. /tmp/recorder-smoke-files-mPZqQW/SystemSketch/recordings/2026-09-01_22-26-25-cable-landed-then-the-detector-w/playback.html  — open in a browser: slow frames, fast lanes, one scrubber; #t=<ms> deep-links a moment.

4 · Using it

Once, after merging

The running desktop windows were started before the debugging port existed, so the first save on them will say frames: canvas only and the packet will say why. One relaunch fixes it:

cd ~/systemsketch && npm run desktop:stop && npm run desktop:preview && npm run desktop:start

Preview's host restarts on its own the next time it is opened, because server.py changed and the controller fingerprint with it.

Every time

Something odd happens → </> → Save the last 30 s (type a line into What went wrong? first if you like) → paste into the agent. The paste is prose plus absolute paths; the agent Reads README.md, greps timeline.jsonl, opens the frames it needs. Copy last recording refills the clipboard after a reload. For a bug you can reproduce, Record next ≤ 30 s, do it, stop or let the cap stop it. Open any folder's playback.html to watch it yourself.

5 · Not done, and the branch

  • Step 7 stays parked, as you asked: replay-to-test and the Chrome trace export.
  • The screencast numbers are headless. A windowed, GPU-backed measurement would be the next honest data point if the desktop ever feels heavier while recording.
  • No merge. The work is on claude/state-recorder-design-95c0fc at a3cf021, with main merged in, pushed to origin. From your checkout: git merge --ff-only claude/state-recorder-design-95c0fc.
